name: インド料理 ルーパリ 若草町店（本店） (Indo Ryori Roopali Wakakusacho-ten (Honten))

claims.text: Naan and the bread-based sets are wheat; in a shared Indian kitchen with flour and fried items, cross-contact with wheat is likely and no gluten-free handling is documented.

Vegetable pakora is fried alongside paneer (cheese) pakora, and curries/naan commonly use ghee, butter, cream or yogurt, so plant-based dishes may share oil and dairy unless you ask staff to omit them.
Genuine meat-free items exist, including vegetable salad with beans, vegetable pakora, and vegetable/chickpea-style curries, so vegetarians have real choices.

name: 板蕎麦 香り家 京橋店 (Itasoba Kaoriya Kyobashi-ten)

claims.text: The dipping sauces are soy-sauce and dashi based; standard Japanese soy sauce contains wheat.

name: 伊都岐珈琲 宮島店 (Itsuki Coffee Miyajima)

claims.text: An English menu is available, which helps travelers communicate basic preferences when ordering.

name: 厳島BARL 厳齋 (Itsukushima BARL Issai)

claims.text: A vegetarian menu is listed as available, so there are at least some meat-free options on offer.
Anago-meshi is served with a glaze/tare conventionally made from wheat-containing soy sauce, and the menu also includes udon (wheat noodles); no gluten-free preparation is documented.
The kitchen is built entirely around conger eel and fish/dashi-based rice bowls and udon; no plant-only preparation is documented and cross-contact with fish is effectively unavoidable.
The bean paste filling is made simply from carefully selected Hokkaido azuki beans and white granulated sugar, with no documented additives.
Shellfish sashimi and grilled shellfish are served and seasoned in the Japanese style, which standardly uses wheat-based soy sauce; no gluten-free soy sauce is mentioned.
The kitchen is entirely shellfish- and seafood-based (oysters, shellfish sashimi, fish/shellfish dashi), so any plant items would share equipment with seafood.

name: 牡蠣フライ串と麦酒 (Kaki Fry Kushi to Bakushu)

claims.text: Core menu is breaded, deep-fried oyster skewers; coating is wheat flour and panko and items are fried in shared oil, so cross-contamination is inherent and unavoidable here.
All offerings are oyster (shellfish) or anago (eel) based and fried in the same oil; there are no plant-based items.
